reason: The Government adopted the Strategy in September 2023, as the Commission confirms. The Commission reported in 2025 that the Government continued to implement it, with tangible progress on all key performance indicators, and the Government's 2025 progress report counts nine actions completed. Implementation of the Strategy as a whole says nothing yet about its results, which depend on its individual measures.

The Commission confirms that the EVO application was launched in June 2024 and EVO 2.0 in June 2026, and that the EVO portal lists 636 public services, 447 of them online. Figures on use (169,692 downloads and 66,733 active users by the end of 2025) come only from the Government's own machine-translated progress report, so use at scale is not independently corroborated.

The CERT directorate was set up by Government Decision No. 1028/2023, and the Commission states that it became fully operational in 2025 and that its cyber incident management platform is installed and used by the team. The Agency's own report records 40 incidents and 52 early warnings in 2025, so the Commission's account is matched by evidence of incidents actually handled.

The Commission and SIGMA describe the portal as the working single point of access to public services, and the Government reports over 0.5 million unique visitors a year and user satisfaction in its annual national survey. Material in the Government's own implementation programme says only a minority of listed services can be completed fully online, the Commission notes the portal is not integrated with EU systems, and by 2026 services are listed on the integrated EVO portal.

The Commission reports that a national digital identity wallet was launched within the EVO application in June 2024. The wallet aligned with the EU Digital Identity framework is a further version: the Government says development started in September 2025, the Commission reports cross-border interoperability tests in 2026, and the Reform Agenda sets its launch for December 2026.

The Commission confirms that 83 centres were set up in 2023, that the network reached 105 by 2025 and 118 by 2026, giving rural residents access to electronic public services. None of the items on the centres gives the number of people served through them, so use at scale is not shown.

The Commission counts MPay among the government platforms Moldova has implemented, and the Digital Public Administration Factsheet describes it as in place since 2020. SIGMA found in 2023 that online payment through MPay was possible but not yet integrated into digital service provision, and the Government's figures on savings and on payments collected through MPay are not corroborated by an independent source.

The new system has not yet been built: the Commission asked in 2025 for its design and development to be sped up and in 2026 still described the existing MTender system as outdated. Government monitoring records that procurement of the developer was published in December 2025 with bids due in February 2026, and the Reform Agenda sets a pilot of the essential modules by December 2027.

The Decision was adopted in November 2019 and applied from 2020, and SIGMA confirms that the e-Governance Agency coordinates ICT procurement plans under it. The Court of Accounts found that the Agency issued 689 opinions on ICT procurement procedures, but also found gaps in application, including bodies outside its scope and donated systems; these audit findings are machine-translated and so of Medium confidence.

The Commission states that MTender has enabled electronic procurement since its launch, with public access to documents, and the Digital Public Administration Factsheet says all public tenders are published on it. The Commission also finds it outdated and not covering the full procurement cycle, and a replacement system is being procured.

The World Bank-supported project was carried out by the e-Governance Agency and concluded in 2025, with the Government reporting 110 digitalised services and 94 re-engineered services. All figures on its delivery and results come from the Government and the Agency, without independent corroboration.

The regulator held the 2024 competition, announced the results in January 2025 and issued the licences to three operators in February 2025, and held a further competition in 2025 that awarded spectrum to Moldtelecom. All items come from the regulator's and the Government's own machine-translated reports, so the status rests on Medium confidence evidence and reported coverage gains are not independently corroborated.

The Commission reported in 2024 that an action plan for joining EURES had been drafted and the National Employment Agency designated. By 2026 it records a Government Decision of September 2025 setting the national framework, an Agency order of November 2025 on the National Coordination Office, ten territorial EURES members and technical standards for matching with the EURES portal; joining itself happens only on accession.

The Commission counts MCloud among the government platforms Moldova has implemented, and RUSI notes that e-government services have adopted cloud solutions such as MCloud. The Court of Accounts found information systems developed without alignment with MCloud and other government platforms, and none of the linked items measures independently how far the platform is used.

The draft law transposing the Data Governance Act was prepared and sent for interinstitutional examination in October 2025, and the data protection authority commented on it in 2026. The Government's 2025 progress report records the action as suspended until 2027 under the National Accession Programme; the draft was not withdrawn, so it remains a proposal.

The Government reports that the e-APL portal was developed and launched as a pilot, with 91 mayoralties taking part and nine State Fiscal Register services available through it. The target is use by at least half of first-level local authorities, and all items come from the Government's own machine-translated documents, so the status rests on Medium confidence evidence.

The Commission describes an electronic cadastral system maintained by the Public Services Agency, through which ownership rights are registered via its offices and online systems, and the Government states that the Real Estate Register is digitalised. Modernisation and a new information system are planned, with re-engineering of cadastral services set for 2026.

The Commission found no progress on aligning with the 5G Cybersecurity Toolbox in 2024, and in 2026 still called on Moldova to start implementing its measures, including restrictions on high-risk suppliers. Alignment of the legal framework and a supplier risk assessment are commitments under the Reform Agenda.

The Commission noted in 2025 that legislative work to align with the Digital Services Act had started, and the Government's 2025 progress report says the draft law is still being prepared with EU4Digital experts. The Government's own accession programme notes that the law has not yet been adopted.

The Law has been in force since 2010 and was amended in 2023 to let EU citizens work for 90 days in any 180 without a permit; otherwise EU and other foreign citizens need a temporary residence permit for work under it. The Commission records 10,290 residence permits granted in 2025, and a draft law on the admission and stay of foreigners would repeal it on entry into force. The Government items are machine-translated.

The Cyber Security Agency reports that most actions in its 2025 plan were fully implemented and some partly or carried over, mainly because of resource constraints and pending regulation. The Commission confirms that the Agency became operational in 2025, but the account of the plan's delivery is the Agency's own and is machine-translated.

The Commission reports that Moldova benefited from several EU4Digital components and pilots, including mutual recognition of electronic signatures with Ukraine, eDelivery and eCustoms. The Government reports continuing EU4Digital technical assistance in 2025 for transposing the EU Digital Identity framework.

The Commission found in 2024 and 2025 that no integrated health information system was in place and recommended developing one, and the Reform Agenda commits Moldova to an eHealth strategy and legal framework. A stakeholder comment in the Government's draft implementation programme refers to such a system as already implemented, but gives no detail and is not corroborated.

The remote identification service has not been launched: the Government reports that the World Bank-supported contract for developing it was signed at the end of 2025 and that the project is in an advanced stage of technical development. All items come from the Government's own documents, mostly machine-translated.

Government Decision No. 860/2024 set the list of critical sectors, and the Cyber Security Agency reports that it sent 307 notifications and issued 265 individual acts designating essential and important service providers in 2025. The figures come only from the Agency's own machine-translated report.

The Commission reports that the National Employment Agency developed a new integrated information system in December 2025, aiming at fully digitalised services by 2027, while the Agency's own 2025 report says the lack of a modern information system affects its services. Neither source says whether the new system is in use, and data exchange with EURES is still being prepared.

The draft law amending the Cybersecurity Law to transpose NIS 2 is listed in the National Accession Programme, and the Reform Agenda treats its adoption as a future step. The Government's 2025 progress report still refers to the amendments as proposed changes, so the draft has not been adopted.

RUSI reports that the EU launched the programme in May 2022, and the Commission records a EUR 235,000 donation of equipment and licences under its second phase. The Government credits it with accelerating cyber resilience, which is its own assessment.

The Court of Accounts found in 2024 that two tenders to draft the methodology produced no winner and the activity was dropped from the World Bank project. The Government's implementation programme plans it again, and its 2025 progress report says completion is pushed to the fourth quarter of 2026; these items are machine-translated.

The Law is in force and sets the rules for access to employment services and measures, which the territorial employment offices apply. Government documents note its gaps, including the exclusion of foreigners with residence for work or study and no rules for EU jobseekers or frontier workers, which a draft amending law addresses; these items are machine-translated.

The Agency's 2025 activity report presents EURES preparation and an integrated labour market information system among the objectives it pursued in 2025 and repeats them for 2026. The Commission confirms the Agency's EURES preparation steps in 2025, while the integrated information system is not yet shown to be in use.
In 2023 IPRE and SIGMA described the free smartphone-based signature as still being prepared, with audit procedures and launch outstanding.
A search of all the country's items found no mention of MobiSign after 2023, so no source says whether it was launched, renamed or dropped.

The Commission reported in 2023 that a further 42 public services had been integrated with MDelivery, which delivers requested documents to the user's home, and the Government lists it among platforms delivered under the modernisation project. The linked items give no figures on its use.

The Commission reports in 2024, 2025 and 2026 that negotiations of social security agreements with further Member States have been initiated and should continue, and records a new agreement with Slovakia in 2026. The negotiations are therefore under way, with more agreements still to conclude.

The Commission confirms that a sub-council on AI and data was set up within the National Digitalisation Council, and the Government reports that it was created in 2024 and contributed to the White Book on AI and Data Governance and to drafting the national AI programme. The body is set up and working, but there is no independent evidence of its influence.
The Commission confirms that the National Cybersecurity Programme 2026-2030 was adopted in December 2025. The linked items do not yet report on its implementation, which began only in 2026.

The Decision of December 2023 established the Cyber Security Agency. The Commission states that the Agency became operational as the national single point of contact and CERT, and the Agency reports exercising its powers, including 265 designations of service providers in 2025.

The National Employment Agency signed cooperation agreements on the labour market inclusion of refugees and vulnerable groups with several organisations between 2023 and 2025. The items record only the signing, from the Agency's and the Migration Inspectorate's own machine-translated reports, and not what the agreements delivered.

The Digital Public Administration Factsheet says the national framework follows the European Interoperability Framework, but the Government notes that the Interoperable Europe Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/903, has not been transposed. Further alignment is planned in the National Accession Programme; these Government items are machine-translated.
Until August 2026 the Law was the general personal data protection law, applied by the data protection authority in the cases it examined in 2025.

The Law was repealed when Law No. 195/2024, which transposes the GDPR, entered into force on 23 August 2026, so it was replaced by newer law rather than abandoned as a policy. The data protection authority notes that its repeal leaves no special law transposing the Law Enforcement Directive.

The Cyber Security Agency reports courses for its own technical staff and thematic courses for CSIRT and public institution staff in 2025, so training has started on a small scale. A comment in the Government's draft implementation programme notes that it contains no specific actions for training civil servants, and all items are the Government's own machine-translated documents.

The regulator reports that the World Bank project is under way and due to finish in 2026, and that broadband networks have been mapped and uncovered areas identified. The status rests only on the regulator's own machine-translated annual report.

Government Decision No. 563/2025 approving the methodological rules for the open data law was adopted in September 2025, as Promo-LEX confirms. The linked items do not report how the rules are applied.

The Commission found in 2024 and 2025 that no national health insurance card exists because there is no integrated health information system. A search of all the country's items for the card found no plan, decision or later finding, so no status can be given.

The Commission's 2024 Communication set out the Growth Plan, and the Reform Agenda for 2025-2027 was agreed under it, with the Government aligning its digital programme to it. The Commission has since approved releases of funds after assessing reform steps, such as the operational national CERT and the roaming acquis.

A grant agreement with Swedfund, approved by ministerial order in March 2025, funds the impact and risk study for the 5G Cybersecurity Toolbox, and the Government's 2025 progress report says KPMG AB is carrying it out. The status rests only on the Government's own machine-translated documents, and the study is not yet complete.

The Commission records TAIEX training for the Cyber Security Agency and its CERT team with Romanian experts, and the regulator reports TAIEX missions and workshops in 2025 on open internet access, roaming and the Gigabit Infrastructure Act.

The Commission reports that Moldova's first European Digital Innovation Hub was launched in April 2026, after the e-Governance Agency prepared the national consortium and application in 2025. The linked items do not yet report on its activity.

The Decision regulates the MConnect interoperability platform, and SIGMA reports 665.7 million transactions through it in 2022, so it is applied at scale. The Government states that data exchange takes place exclusively through MConnect, but the data protection authority finds that state bodies continue to access personal data through another technology, so how fully the Decision is applied is disputed.

Training of employment agency staff on EURES and on serving EU citizens under Law No. 200/2025 is planned in the National Accession Programme. A search of all the country's items found no record that this training has taken place; the Commission notes in 2026 only that the Agency focused on staff training, without saying on what. The Government items are machine-translated.

The Law was adopted on 17 April 2025, the Commission assessed that Moldova's legislation correctly transposed the whole EU roaming acquis, and Moldova joined the Roam Like at Home area on 1 January 2026. The linked items give no data yet on roaming use under the new regime.

The Government reports that the Directorate for policies on information technology and digitalisation exists within the Ministry, with nine of its ten posts filled and only a few staff per policy area. The status rests on the Government's own machine-translated account.

The data protection authority states that people can consult the history of access to their personal data, drawn from MLog, through a government portal, and the Digital Public Administration Factsheet describes MLog as a logbook of actions in government systems. The linked items do not measure how widely it is used.

The regulator reports that it signed Working Arrangements with BEREC in March 2025, giving it participant status without voting rights. Its participation in three BEREC working groups is planned from 2026, and all items are the regulator's own machine-translated report.

CSO Meter reports that the register is still the system through which non-commercial organisations are registered, but that it is outdated, not interoperable and slows down registration. A new State Register of Legal Units is being developed but is not yet operational.

The Commission confirms that amendments to the law on the regime of foreigners entered into force in January 2024, allowing EU citizens and those of some other countries to work in Moldova without a work permit. The linked items do not report how many EU citizens have worked under these rules.

The Commission reports in 2026 that implementation of the 2030 national health strategy progressed, with a focus on digital transformation and quality of care. It had earlier asked for the strategy to be implemented effectively, including an integrated e-health system, which is still not in place.

Development of networks in white areas is planned in the digital strategy's implementation programme, and the Government's 2025 progress report says it can start only after the regulator's geographic survey under the new Electronic Communications Law and the broadband mapping system. The items are machine-translated.

A draft order on standard contractual clauses is listed in the National Accession Programme. The Commission asked in 2025 for the legal framework to be adopted, and the data protection authority repeated that call in its 2025 activity report, so it had not been adopted by then.

A draft law on horizontal cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements is listed in the National Accession Programme, and the Reform Agenda describes these requirements as future measures.

The Commission records that the regulator, the Agency for Geodesy, Cartography and Cadastre and the national cadastre entered into a trilateral agreement on 18 March 2026 to share spatial datasets for the very high capacity network map. The linked items do not yet report the map itself.

The Commission reports that the new legislation opened certain technical, specialised and auxiliary public administration positions to EU citizens, while civil servant posts remain restricted to Moldovan nationals. The linked items do not report EU citizens recruited to these posts.

The Government reports that the Code of Contraventions was amended to set fines for breaches of the data exchange and interoperability law, effective from 18 January 2021. The linked items do not report any fines imposed.

The Cyber Security Agency reports that it records cyber incidents in a register, 40 by the end of 2025, and reports incidents with significant impact on critical infrastructure to the Intelligence and Security Service. The Commission confirms that 38 incidents were handled in 2025, but the reporting obligations on providers are described only by the Agency.

The targets come from the Digital Transformation Strategy adopted in 2023, which aims for all key public services to be online by 2030, and the Government repeats them in 2025 and 2026. The Commission reports that 447 of 636 services, 70.3%, were online in 2026.

Government Decision No. 860/2024 lists the critical sectors and types of providers, and the Cyber Security Agency reports using it to identify and designate essential and important service providers, with 265 designation acts issued in 2025. The account of its application is the Agency's own machine-translated report.

The National Accession Programme plans a support unit for opening data in the e-Governance Agency and a reporting system for public authorities. The Government's 2025 progress report records only that one open data specialist post was created, so the unit and the reporting system are not yet in place. The linked items are machine-translated.

The Government lists the Central Electoral Commission's prior registration service for voters abroad, electronic subscription lists and electronic complaints module as implemented, following amendments to the Electoral Code. The status rests only on the Government's machine-translated account, with no data on use.

A draft Government Decision creating a national e-Health entity and its operation as the health data access body are planned in the National Accession Programme. The linked items do not record its creation. The linked items are machine-translated.

The Government lists MNotify among the reusable platforms developed and implemented, and states that public bodies must use it exclusively for electronic notifications. The linked items give no figures on its use, and these items are machine-translated.

Government Decision No. 534/2025 approved the concept of the eNotariat information system, and the Government reports that the EBRD is funding its development and launched procurement in March 2025. The system is not yet reported as built, and the items are machine-translated.

The Decision grants temporary protection with the right to work, and the employment agency reports 1,598 notifications of employment of displaced Ukrainians under it. The ETF policy brief confirms that refugees with temporary protection work in practice, although often below their skills.

Freedom House reported in 2024 that the regulator had begun preparing to license the 5G frequency bands. The process led to the 2024 competition, whose results were announced in January 2025, with licences issued to three operators in February 2025.
Freedom House described this Law in 2024 as the framework for electronic communications, with ANRCETI as regulator.

The new Electronic Communications Law No. 72/2025 entered into force on 1 January 2026, as the Commission confirms, and the regulator was renamed under it. None of the linked items states the repeal of the earlier law in terms, but the new law has replaced it as the sector framework, which is a replacement rather than a policy reversal.

The Government lists particip.gov.md among the platforms implemented, and CSO Meter notes continued government improvements to it as part of implementing the open data law. The linked items give no figures on its use.

The Commission reported in 2021 that the Ministry had adopted the roadmap, and the Government states that substantial legislative amendments were promoted on its basis. The account of its delivery is the Government's own and machine-translated.

The Commission reported in 2023 that no electronic biometric database existed and that developing one had been set as an objective. The National Accession Programme still plans a system for capturing biometric data at border crossing points, so the database is not reported as built.

The Commission asked in 2023 for Moldova to connect to TESTA, and the National Accession Programme plans the connection, with the number of public entities connected as its indicator. The linked items do not record the connection.

The Commission reported in 2023 that Moldova continued aligning its cybersecurity legislation with the NIS Directive, and RUSI reports legislation requiring critical infrastructure providers to adopt prescribed security measures. This alignment work is reflected in Cybersecurity Law No. 48/2023, which is now being amended to transpose NIS 2.

SIGMA reports that the register was established in 2021 and covers about 718 public services, and the Commission states that it was used to map administrative services and support their re-engineering.
The Commission reports that Moldova takes part as an observer in Technical Support Instrument pilot projects, two in 2024 and three in 2025.

The Commission confirms that the Agency was set up on 1 January 2025 with a mandate for justice sector information systems. It asked in 2025 for its operationalisation to be sped up and found in 2026 that its capacity remains extremely limited because of staffing problems.

The Commission reports that Moldova harmonised its framework with the Gigabit Infrastructure Act through Law No. 106 on access to property, adopted in June 2026. The linked items do not yet report how the law is applied.

The Reform Agenda and the National Accession Programme planned to establish the National Contact Point for eHealth by December 2025. A search of all the country's items found no record that it has been established.

The Cyber Security Agency reports that cooperation with the OSCE provided technical equipment for its operation. The Commission's item on donated equipment names the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency and Halo Trust rather than the OSCE, so the OSCE contribution rests on the Agency's machine-translated report alone.

The draft law on the digitalisation of judicial cooperation is listed in the National Accession Programme, and the Commission reports that normative amendments promoting the digitalisation of certain judicial procedures were made in August 2026. The Commission does not name the act, so the match with this draft is probable but not confirmed.

The Commission reports that the Migration Inspectorate approved the procedure in March 2026 and that 28 applications for residence documents had been submitted under it. Use is so far small, with 422 EU citizens still documented under the old regime in 2025.

The Commission reports that the National Employment Agency developed a new integrated information system in December 2025, aiming at fully digitalised services by 2027, and a 2026 Government document says the system, funded by the EU Delegation, is still being developed. Neither source reports it in use.
Modernisation, automation and interoperability of state registers are planned in the 2023 Digital Transformation Strategy and in the National Accession Programme. The items describe plans only.

The Decision approved the concept and regulation of the register of state information resources and systems, and the e-Governance Agency has adjusted its documentation. SIGMA states that all state information resources and systems have been registered, while the Court of Accounts finds their registration delayed, so how fully the register is used is disputed.

The Digital Public Administration Factsheet describes SIVE as an online platform for registering and processing requests for energy compensation, and the Court of Accounts examined how it was procured. The linked items give no figures on its use.

The Government reports that Law No. 321/2023 set the framework for stimulating electronic services, including the digital identity card, driving licence and registration certificate. The linked items do not report specifically on its application.

The Migration Inspectorate reports that Government Decision No. 618/2023 approved the concept of its information system, after an assessment of its digitalisation needs. The linked items do not report the system itself as built. The linked items are machine-translated.

Law No. 200/2025 gives the Equality Council competence to promote and monitor equal treatment of EU citizens and to act as national contact point. Amendments to the Council's own law to carry out these tasks are still in draft, and the linked items do not report the Council acting in this role. The linked items are machine-translated.

The National Accession Programme says the Ministry of Internal Affairs will determine how arriving Member State citizens are registered and that the Migration Inspectorate will take measures to inform and refer them. The items describe plans only. The linked items are machine-translated.

The National Accession Programme plans amendments to the health care and compulsory health insurance laws for 2025 and 2026, including to introduce the European Health Insurance Card. The Commission reports only a feasibility study on the card, finalised in August 2026, so the amendments are not reported as adopted.

Training of public authority and Equality Council staff on equal treatment of EU workers under Law No. 200/2025 is planned in the National Accession Programme. The items describe plans only. The linked items are machine-translated.

The regulator adopted detailed rules on fair use and on the sustainability of retail roaming at domestic prices in 2025. The Commission assessed the amended secondary legislation as correctly transposing the roaming acquis, and the rules have applied since Moldova joined Roam Like at Home on 1 January 2026.
Designation of the market surveillance authority under the Cyber Resilience Act is planned in the National Accession Programme. The items describe plans only. The linked items are machine-translated.

The draft Government Decision on coordinated vulnerability disclosure is listed in the National Accession Programme. The linked items do not record its adoption. The linked items are machine-translated.

Access to the AGORA information exchange system is foreseen in the National Accession Programme. Comments recorded in it point out that the draft digital services law does not provide for cooperation through AGORA, which is open only to Member States, so access is not yet possible. The linked items are machine-translated.

The data protection authority operates under this Law and had 36 staff at the end of 2025, nine short of its staffing limit. The Government lists the Law among the acts making up the framework until the new data protection law entered into force in August 2026, and the linked items do not say whether it remains in force since then.

The Government states that its temporary protection framework is aligned with Directive 2001/55/EC and that it will align with Decision (EU) 2025/1460 extending protection until 1 March 2027. A search of all the country's items found no record of the extension being adopted, and both statements are the Government's own and machine-translated.

The National Accession Programme says the National Visa Information System needs to be made operational and interoperable with the EU Visa Information System, and lists a draft Government Decision for it. The items describe plans only. The linked items are machine-translated.

The Migration Inspectorate sent proposals in January 2025 to amend the Decision in line with Eurodac, and the National Accession Programme plans interoperability of the Fingerprint Register with Eurodac. No adoption of the amendments is recorded in these items. The linked items are machine-translated.

The Government says the intellectual property agency uses online platforms for electronic filing, but the National Accession Programme sets developing, testing and launching the e-AGEPI system as a future target. The items do not make clear whether e-AGEPI is the existing platform or a new system. The linked items are machine-translated.

The Digital Public Administration Factsheet describes the e-Invoice service on the Electronic Fiscal Services platform, and the Government's implementation programme gives 64% of companies using electronic invoices. The usage figure is the Government's own, machine-translated and not independently corroborated.

Drafting a law to transpose the e-Commerce Directive is planned in the digital strategy's implementation programme, and the Government's 2025 progress report says full alignment will be ensured through the draft law on digital services, which is still being drafted. The linked items are machine-translated.

The amending law is planned in the digital strategy's implementation programme, and the Government's 2025 progress report says the start of drafting was announced on particip.gov.md on 3 February 2026. The linked items are machine-translated.

The Digital Public Administration Factsheet lists the State Population Register as one of the two basic state information resources under Law No. 467/2003, and the implementation programme plans its modernisation. The linked items give no figures on its use.

The Government's 2025 progress report says that, on the advice of DG CNECT, inclusion of STISC in the EU trusted list must be preceded by a conformity audit, and that STISC is taking the measures needed to organise it. The audit has not yet taken place. The linked items are machine-translated.
Draft laws refer to Law No. 121/2012 as the law in force that sets the grounds of discrimination. The linked items do not report how the Law is applied. The linked items are machine-translated.

RUSI reports that the Estonian eGovernance Academy has supported legislative, strategic and organisational reforms over the past decade, and the Cyber Security Agency reports continuing support for its development and training in 2025.
The regulator reports 36 inspections of electronic communications and postal services in 2025 and the main violations found. The figures are the regulator's own and machine-translated.

IPRE cites STISC data that in September 2022 only 66 of about 129,000 active qualified signature certificates were on eID cards issued by the Public Services Agency, so the cards existed but were barely used for signing. The linked item gives no later figures.
The only linked item is an IPRE recommendation to develop free internet access points on the WiFi4EU model. It does not show whether Moldova takes part in WiFi4EU.
Freedom House states that Moldova enforces Convention 108 and other international agreements to which it is a party. The statement is general and gives no evidence of application.
CSO Meter reports that the Ombudsman made guaranteeing human rights in digitalisation and the use of AI a strategic priority. The linked item does not report any action taken under it.

CSO Meter describes the Law on Access to Information of Public Interest as aligned with EU standards and improving proactive publication and open data. This is an assessment of the Law's content; the linked item does not report its application.
The Commission reports that Moldova was granted access to Tenders Electronic Daily in October 2020 and that its contracting authorities can publish contract notices in the Official Journal of the EU.

The Commission reports that the Regulation obliges contracting authorities to carry out all stages of most low-value procurement through the State Register of Public Procurement. The linked item does not report its application.
The Commission asked in 2023 for Moldova to connect to CECIS through TESTA, and the National Accession Programme plans the TESTA connection. No connection is recorded in these items.
The Commission states that Moldova is kept informed through the Animal Disease Information System about outbreaks in the EU and follows these reports for imports of animal products.

The Commission reported in 2024 that Moldova proposed to upgrade its agreement with Italy, then that an agreement with Italy was signed in October 2024 and entered into force in September 2025; the social insurance office lists it with its administrative arrangement and forms. The Commission does not say in terms that the signed agreement is the proposed upgrade.

The Commission reports that Moldova adopted a series of business facilitation packages and reduced the regulatory and administrative burden on business. The linked item gives no detail on their application.

The Commission's 2024 Communication tied the Facility's investment to implementation of the Reform Agenda, and the Commission has since adopted implementing decisions releasing funds after assessing reform steps such as the operational national CERT and the roaming acquis.

The Commission's 2025 finding that interoperability between automated verification systems and state registries must still be strengthened shows the systems are in place. It also finds them insufficiently connected and the services understaffed.
The Commission reports that asset declarations will now be published in open data format and stored for 15 years. The linked item does not report publication in practice.
The Commission reports that the social security agreement with France was signed in March 2025. The Commission's 2026 report records the Italian agreement's entry into force but not the French one's.
The Commission reports a monitoring mission's finding that technical arrangements for ICS2 are pending implementation.
The Reform Agenda commits the incumbent operator to implement network-sharing agreements in line with the Gigabit Infrastructure Act. The linked item records the commitment only.

The only linked item is a Reform Agenda target for the integrated case management system to cover all cases and connect with seven information systems. It shows that the target is not yet met but not the system's current state.

The Commission reports that the online beneficial ownership declaration service was developed on the Digital Services Development Platform and is available to the public through the Public Services Portal and the Public Services Agency portal. The linked item gives no figures on its use.
The Commission reports that the EcoAlert platform, where citizens can report environmental issues, was established at ecoalert.md. The linked item gives no figures on its use.

The Commission reports that in February 2026 Moldova designated the National Office of Social Insurance and the National Health Insurance Company as liaison bodies, and the e-Governance Agency as EESSI access point. The linked item does not report them acting in that role.

The Commission reports that Moldova developed a national strategy to align with eIDAS 2.0, including the EU Digital Identity Wallet, and joined the EU Digital Identity Cooperation Group. It does not say whether the strategy was formally adopted.
The Commission reports that the methodological rules on the use of the Anti-Fraud Information System were approved in September 2026.
The 2023 Digital Transformation Strategy proposes a governance and coordination structure under the Ministry. The linked item describes the proposal only.
The 2023 Digital Transformation Strategy lists automatic decision-making in the public sector as a line of action. The linked item describes the plan only.

The 2023 Strategy states that STISC manages the Government's public key infrastructure, and IPRE cites STISC data of about 129,000 active qualified signature certificates in 2022. The figures come from STISC itself.
